docs.title: Ragdoll (Reusable Abstraction Language Layer for General-purpose & Domain-Oriented Computing)
docs.text:
The title RAGDOLL encapsulates the project's ambition to serve as a versatile, high-performance toolkit for the research community, offering both general and specialized computing capabilities through its unique language architecture. Specifically:

  • Research: Signifies the project's focus on advanced computing fields such as scientific computing, numerical computing, and other specialized areas, indicating its suitability for cutting-edge research and development.
  • Assemble: Highlights the comprehensive and integrative approach of the project, bringing together various computing paradigms and tools under one umbrella.
  • General-purpose and Domain-Oriented: Reflects the dual nature of the project's language offerings, catering both to broad computing needs and to niche, specialized requirements.
  • Computing Language Layer: Indicates the project's foundation or platform nature, providing a base upon which diverse computational tasks can be performed, facilitated by the tailored languages it supports.

Domain-specific computing focuses on developing computational tools and techniques tailored for specific fields or applications, such as bioinformatics, finance, or image processing. This specialization enables more efficient and effective solutions to complex, domain-specific problems. However, the power of domain-specific computing is significantly enhanced by leveraging generalized techniques. For instance, probabilistic programming allows for flexible modeling of uncertainty, which is a common aspect across many fields. It enables domain experts to build complex statistical models without delving into the intricacies of underlying algorithms. Automatic differentiation, another versatile technique, streamlines the computation of gradients, which are crucial in optimization problems prevalent in various domains, from machine learning to engineering design. Reversible transformations offer efficient memory use in simulations, which is beneficial in fields like physics or chemistry simulations. These general techniques not only provide a robust foundation for building domain-specific tools but also facilitate cross-domain knowledge transfer, enhancing innovation and efficiency in specialized computing tasks. Thus, the synergy between domain-specific focus and general-purpose computational techniques leads to a more powerful and versatile technology landscape.

We hereby present Ragdoll, representing an assembled language layer for Domain-specific Computing with tons of performance optimisations, which builds domain-specific languages atop of generalised computing paradigms, include AutoDiff, ProbProgramming, Automatic Reversible Transformations, and so on. In general, Ragdoll is featured with:

  • Automatic Differentiation
  • (WIP) Probablistic Pogramming
  • (WIP) Automatic Reversible Transformations
  • (WIP) Automatic Fusion
  • (WIP) Cache Reuse Optimisations
  • (WIP) High abstraction level symbolic optimisations
  • (WIP) Leverage the kernel generation with IREE system

docs.title: Config-driven Benchmarking System
docs.text:
如何优化他们的配置系统，特别是关于工作负载（workload）的类型设计。他们当前的配置使用了workload_granularity、model_workload和op_workload来处理模型和算子的benchmark功能，但觉得这样的设计可能不够简洁和优雅，类型系统看起来有些复杂。用户希望找到一种更简便、清晰的设计方式，使类型系统更清爽。

首先，我需要回顾用户当前的配置结构。他们有一个Config类，其中包含多个枚举字段，如workload_type（可能是模型或算子）、workload_granularity（工作负载的粒度）、model_workload（具体模型类型）和op_workload（具体算子类型）。这种设计将工作负载的类型和具体实现分开，但可能导致配置时需要同时设置多个相关字段，增加了复杂性。

用户提到系统需要兼容对算子负载和模型负载的benchmark功能，这意味着需要根据不同的负载类型选择具体的模型或算子。当前的设计可能让用户在使用时需要同时处理多个字段，容易出现不一致的情况，例如选择了模型负载但未指定具体模型，或者同时指定了模型和算子导致冲突。

接下来，我需要思考如何简化这一设计。可能的思路是采用继承或组合的方式，将工作负载相关的配置封装到一个单独的类或结构中。例如，引入一个Workload基类，然后派生出ModelWorkload和OpWorkload子类，每个子类包含特定于该类型负载的配置项。这样，Config类中只需包含一个workload字段，根据负载类型动态选择相应的子类，从而减少冗余字段，并提高类型系统的清晰度。

另一个可能的优化点是使用联合类型（Union Types）或代数数据类型（ADTs），例如Python 3.10引入的TypeAlias和Union，或者使用@dataclass的嵌套结构。这样可以在类型系统中明确表示工作负载只能是模型或算子中的一种，避免同时设置多个不相关的字段。

此外，用户当前的代码中使用了多个枚举类型来区分不同的负载类型和具体实现，这可能导致枚举类过多，维护起来较为复杂。可以考虑将这些枚举合并或重构为更简洁的结构，例如使用字符串字面量类型或字典映射，减少类的数量，同时保持类型安全。

还需要考虑YAML配置文件的解析如何适应新的设计。新的设计应该使得配置文件的结构更直观，用户只需在YAML中指定工作负载类型（如model或op），然后提供相应的参数，而不需要处理多个可能冲突的字段。例如，YAML中可以有一个workload字段，其子字段根据类型不同而不同，这样解析时可以根据类型动态加载相应的配置。

另外，类型提示和静态检查也是需要考虑的因素。新的设计应该利用Python的类型系统，使IDE和静态类型检查工具（如mypy）能够捕获配置错误，例如错误地混合模型和算子的配置参数。通过合理设计数据类，可以在编码阶段就发现潜在的问题，而不是在运行时。

最后，需要评估这种重构对现有系统的影响。用户可能已经有大量的YAML配置文件，需要确保新的设计能够向后兼容，或提供迁移工具帮助用户转换旧的配置文件。同时，确保新的类型系统在代码中的使用方式尽可能简洁，减少修改现有代码的工作量。

总结下来，优化方向可能包括：

  1. 将工作负载配置封装为独立的数据类，使用继承或联合类型。

  2. 合并或简化枚举类型，减少类的数量。

  3. 利用Python的类型提示提高代码的清晰度和安全性。

  4. 设计直观的YAML结构，便于用户理解和维护。

  5. 确保向后兼容性或提供迁移路径。

接下来需要具体实现这些优化点，并验证其是否达到预期的简洁性和优雅性。

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: To get started with the project, follow these steps to set up the Python sandbox environment, install dependencies, build the project, and run tests.

docs.title: 1. Create a Python Sandbox Execution Environment
docs.text:
Start by creating a virtual environment to isolate your project’s dependencies. This ensures that the project uses its own dependencies, avoiding conflicts with other Python projects.

make bootstrap

This will create a Python sandbox, which includes the environment and necessary packages.

docs.title: 2. Activate the Sandbox Environment
docs.text:
Once the sandbox environment is set up, you need to activate it. This is done depending on the shell you are using.

For Bash or Zsh:

source ./sandbox/bin/activate

For C-shell (csh or tcsh):

source ./sandbox/bin/activate.csh

For Fish shell:

source ./sandbox/bin/activate.fish

Activating the environment will ensure that your project uses the correct dependencies installed within the sandbox.

docs.title: 3. Compile Project Dependencies
docs.text:
Before building the project, you need to compile its dependencies, which include LLVM, MLIR, IREE, and other necessary libraries. Use the following command to compile and set up these dependencies:

make setup

This will ensure that all necessary dependencies are compiled and ready for use in the project.

docs.title: 4. Build and Install the Project
docs.text:
Once the dependencies are set up, you can proceed to build the project. This step compiles and prepares the project's source code for use.

This will compile the project, including the core components and any necessary extensions.

After the build completes successfully, the next step is to install the project on your system. This will copy the necessary files and configurations to their appropriate locations for runtime use.

make build

docs.title: 5. Verify the Installation
docs.text:
To verify that the project has been correctly set up, you can run the tests to ensure everything is working as expected. The following command will execute the project’s test suite:

make test

This will run the tests and output the results, allowing you to confirm that the setup and installation were successful.
